meta.title: Hush Studio Build Plan
meta.subtitle: Hush Studio: the recording and render app for the Sam Katz Hypnosis channel. Migrated 2026-11-10 from ops/state.json.

guide.heading: What this is
rows: Task plan for Hush Studio (sound recording app, repo folder pika_meditate). Narthen Control reads and edits this file.
CLAUDE.md is the architectural source of truth. Render speed is the #1 requirement: encode each unique piece once, build the long video by stream-copy.
Docs/Engine Build Plan/engine_plan.json (path kept from Narthen Control's defaults). The workbook is generated from it; never edit the .xlsx directly.

milestones.name: Fix recording quality
milestones.goal: Found in testing 2026-11-10: the audio sounds distorted and has cuts. Nothing else ships until a take records, masters and renders clean.
milestones.exit: Root causes found and fixed; an automated check catches clipping, distortion and dropouts; a real take is verified clean by ear and by test.

milestones.name: Verify and publish
milestones.goal: Prove the shipped pipeline on real material and publish to the real channel account.
milestones.exit: Full pytest green, FINISH timing on Sam's real take recorded, a real YouTube upload tested.

milestones.name: Editing workflow
milestones.goal: Sam can review and adjust everything the auto-editor proposes before render.
milestones.exit: Flub-cut proposals reviewable (accept/undo); induction-phase marker pauses handled.

milestones.name: Takes and editor
milestones.goal: After recording, an Edit button opens an Audacity-style editor so Sam can edit by hand or still use the automated features. Takes are saved, browsable, importable and exportable.
milestones.exit: Takes library with file-explorer view; import/export; in-app waveform editor; open in Audacity at any point.

milestones.name: Publishing and integrations
milestones.goal: Manage intros, set YouTube thumbnails, and connect Riverside and Canva.
milestones.exit: Intros can be uploaded and swapped; thumbnails upload with the video; Riverside and Canva workflows decided and built.

milestones.name: Install, update and diagnostics
milestones.goal: Sam installs the latest build with one download, the app updates itself from GitHub, and every problem she hits leaves logs (and, with her consent, audio) that we can debug from.
milestones.exit: A Setup.exe on GitHub Releases installs on a clean Windows PC; the app offers updates; a debug bundle from her PC can be opened with core.diagnostics.

milestones.name: Later scope
milestones.goal: Features deferred until the recording workflow is solid.

decisions.question: How should the hand-editor work?
decisions.options: Build our own waveform editor in the PyQt app; only hand off to Audacity; both.
decisions.recommendation: Both. A simple in-app editor (select, cut, delete, silence, undo, zoom, play, plus buttons for the automated features) so Sam never leaves the app, and an Open in Audacity round-trip for anything heavier.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Both. A simple in-app editor (select, cut, delete, silence, undo, zoom, play, plus buttons for the automated features) so Sam never leaves the app, and an Open in Audacity round-trip for anything heavier.

decisions.question: How deep should the Riverside integration go?
decisions.options: Drag/watch-folder import of Riverside exports; Riverside API (if her plan includes it); both.
decisions.recommendation: Start with a smooth import of Riverside exports (watch folder + drag-in, auto-detect 44.1 kHz mono). Add the API only if her plan exposes recording downloads.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: let leave this feaute for a future update

decisions.question: How should Canva fit in?
decisions.options: Open Canva with a thumbnail template and import the exported PNG; Canva Connect API (OAuth, export design); both.
decisions.recommendation: Start with open-in-Canva plus importing the exported PNG from a watched folder. Connect API later if Sam wants one-click export from inside the app.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Start with open-in-Canva plus importing the exported PNG from a watched folder. Connect API later if Sam wants one-click export from inside the app.

decisions.question: Where do saved takes live, and what is a take?
decisions.options: Folder per take under a user-chosen Takes folder; single-file bundle; database index.
decisions.recommendation: Folder per take (raw audio, edit list, notes, metadata), in a Takes folder Sam can see in Explorer, with an exported .hushtake zip as the shareable form.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Folder per take (raw audio, edit list, notes, metadata), in a Takes folder Sam can see in Explorer, with an exported .hushtake zip as the shareable form.

decisions.question: Where do installable builds live, and does the source repo stay public?
decisions.options: Releases on the existing public Hush-Studio repo; a separate small public repo that holds only installers (source repo goes private); private repo plus an access token inside the app.
decisions.recommendation: A separate public repo for installers only (for example Hush-Studio-Releases), and make the source repo private. The updater then downloads anonymously with no token. Reason: the source repo is public today and its docs name Sam's channel and her home neighbourhood and default coordinates.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Installers are published in a separate public repo (Hush-Studio-Releases) that holds only builds; the source repo Hush-Studio becomes private. The updater downloads from the releases repo without a token.

decisions.question: How do logs and audio get from Sam's PC to us, and what audio may be captured?
decisions.options: Export a debug bundle zip that Sam sends herself (email or shared drive); upload to a private GitHub repo with a token; automatic upload.
decisions.recommendation: Export a zip she sends herself. Logs and measurements always; audio only as short clips around a problem spot, shown to her and sent only if she ticks a box. Her sessions are client-facing hypnosis recordings, so nothing leaves the PC without her choosing it.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Debug bundle is a zip Sam exports herself and hands over on a flash drive (email or a shared drive also fine). Logs and measurements always; audio only as opt-in clips she ticks. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

tasks.title: Find and fix the distorted audio in recorded takes
tasks.why: Reported from testing 2026-11-10: the output sounds distorted. Cause not yet known.
tasks.scope: Reproduce with a real mic take. Bisect the chain stage by stage (raw capture, denoise, auto-edit/splice, master gain and limiter, AAC encode) by listening to and measuring each stage's output (clipping, peak, THD, spectrum). Candidates to check, unconfirmed: input gain or clipping at capture, denoise artefacts, limiter or gain stage, crossfades at cuts, sample-rate mismatch. Fix the cause; do not mask it.

REVIEW FINDINGS, round 2 (Claude, 2026-11-11):
1) core/denoise.py:288 deepfilter_array: when peak*stage_scale > DFN_HEADROOM the input scale is DFN_HEADROOM/peak/stage_scale; it must be DFN_HEADROOM/peak (so peak*scale = 0.9). Dividing by stage_scale again attenuates the model input far below the raw level (e.g. frozen +24 dB gain from a quiet first live segment, later segment peak 0.5 -> scale ~0.11, ~19 dB quieter than raw), which re-creates the quiet-input cut-off-phrase defect in live REC. Offline whole-file path is unaffected (gain derived from same peak), so add a test with explicit/frozen stage_gain_db and a louder segment asserting the model input peak is ~0.9 and the output is returned to source level.
